findings.title: Slice insertion without a length guard
findings.message: The code assumes at least 3 children and slices children[:3] and children[3:]. A shorter list would panic. In addition, appending to children[:3] writes into the original backing array while the inner append is still reading children[3:]. The inner append copies first, so it works today, but the pattern is fragile.
findings.suggestion: Use slices.Insert(children, 3, spaceNode, flexNode) after checking len(children) >= 3.
findings.evidence: children = append(children[:3], append([]ui.Node{{ID: id + "/space", Kind: ui.ToolbarSpace}, {ID: id + "/flexible-space", Kind: ui.ToolbarFlexibleSpace}}, children[3:]...)...)

findings.title: Flexible space Max of 0 and ignored style overrides
findings.message: The flexible space sets Max.X to 0 and relies on Cogent treating zero as unbounded. The fixed-space sizing is also hardcoded to 16 dp, so the documented MinSize/MaxSize styling of space width is not honored; Styler runs after any style set on the node.
findings.suggestion: Verify that Max.X == 0 means unbounded in Cogent and that node Style overrides are applied. Tests only check that the flexible space is wider than the fixed one, not the actual widths.

findings.title: Redundant map and fragile index coupling
findings.message: Spaces are stored in an extra map and then skipped when building options. But WithToolbarOverflow already turns spaces into Separator options, so a hidden space is meant to be dropped here. The overflow menu no longer reflects hidden spaces, yet the Options-to-children index alignment in the overflow frame (hidden[i]) still counts spaces. This is fragile, and the extra map is redundant.
findings.suggestion: Check ui.IsToolbarSpace directly while iterating, or build options without space entries and keep the index mapping explicit.
